// version: 0.3 because the wrappers now mirror the curated hierarchy (SDK#30) and the
ActiveWeapon/LastWeapon companions retyped EntityWrapper? -> BasePlayerWeapon?.
The retype is a source-compatible narrowing but BINARY-breaking, and no
deprecation shim can carry a property type flip -- the version number is the
only signal there is. Pre-1.0 the minor is where that signal lives. The rest
of the change is additive: 7 classes lost sealed, 51 gained a base type,
CIncendiaryGrenade joined the curated set (the one common weapon class
SDK#34's measurements found missing), and the 46 marker bindings stopped
being empty under the prefix ordinal layout.
Still 0.x, deliberately: 1.0 is the claim that the shape survived contact
with a second implementation, and prefix layout has not -- DemoViewer.NET's
stage-2/3 rerun against THIS release is the standing criterion (SDK#34).
Their measurements motivated the layout (SDK#30 Q2: the wire flattens
exactly the true ancestry), but measuring a synthetic manifest is not
running the shipped one. Cutting 1.0 is a release decision taken after that
rerun, not a side effect of this change.
It does NOT track the family major, and it does not track the abstractions
version either. This regenerates with the schema; the contract does not.
Sharing a number with either would mean one of them moving for a reason that
has nothing to do with it.
// versionHeightOffset: Cancels the commit that changes `version` above, so a MAJOR.MINOR bump cuts a
real X.Y.0. See the root README's versioning section for why every package
Safe to introduce with the initial version rather than alongside a bump,
because nothing is published under this ID yet -- there is no feed entry for
a lower number to hide behind.
// pathFilters: Its own directory. Unlike the abstractions contract next door, this one SHOULD
move when the schema moves: the wrappers are regenerated from
schema-lens/state.json, so a curation change that adds a field is a real change
to this package's surface and should ship as one.
